text: Is the production of knowledge solely due to the concomitance of knowledge accompanied by the absence of defects, or is it due to the concomitance of knowledge accompanied by the absence of defects? The former is not the case, because the production of knowledge due to the concomitance of knowledge accompanied by the absence of defects is established by the proponents of validity (pramāṇavādin) as a subsequent inference. The latter is also not the case, because once the concomitance of the absence of defects with the whole (sāmagrī) is established, the invariable concomitance (anvaya-vyatireka) is established in no other way, and the causality of the absence of defects is rendered ineffective like a coat of varnish. If it is said that absence is not a cause at all, then it must be stated whether absence has an effect or not. If it does not have an effect, then the non-production of the destruction of the pot would imply the eternity of the pot.
